title: Recommendation
description: A single piece of coaching advice bound to one observation.

confidence.description: How confident the coach is in this advice as a whole.

evidence.description: What this advice rests on, split by kind of claim.

game_id.description: Which game this advice is for.

observation_id.description:
The observation this advice describes. The binding that makes staleness
detectable rather than a matter of opinion.

rationale.description: Why, in prose, for a player who wants to understand rather than obey.

session_id.description: Coaching session this advice belongs to.

summary.description: One-line advice, the thing a player reads mid-turn.

validity.description: Conditions under which this advice dies.

warnings.description:
Caveats the player should see alongside the advice, for example that a
field could not be read.

Confidence.description: Confidence in the closed interval 0.0 to 1.0. NaN is not a valid value.

GameId.description:
Stable identifier for a supported game, matching the directory name
under `games/` and the `id` field of that game's `game.yaml`.

A `GameId` value may exist in platform crates; a *literal* game id may
not. The architecture test draws that line.

ObservationId.description:
Identifies one observation of game state.

Load-bearing: every recommendation is bound to the `ObservationId` it
was generated from, and a recommendation whose observation has been
superseded is invalidated rather than shown as current. This is the
identifier that makes "never silently stale" checkable.

RecommendationEvidence.description:
The four-way evidence split.

Each list holds a different *kind* of claim, and the interface renders them
differently because a player should be able to tell "your gold is 7"
(observed) from "opponents are probably ahead on tempo" (inferred). The
recommendation validator rejects any advice whose `strategy_refs` cite a
document that was not retrieved for this turn, which is only checkable
because the citations live in their own list.

model_inferences.description: Claims the model produced that are neither observed nor cited.

observed_facts.description:
Facts read from the observation. Each should be traceable to a field in
the envelope.

strategy_refs.description:
Identifiers of strategy documents retrieved for this turn. Verified
against what retrieval actually returned.

user_provided.description: Context the user supplied, for example an answer to a spoken question.

RecommendedAction.description: One concrete thing the player could do, in priority order.

action.description: Adapter-defined action verb, for example `buy` or `sell`.

condition.description:
A precondition the player should check first, when the advice is
conditional. Absent means unconditional, not "unknown".

SessionId.description:
Identifies one coaching session: a run of the app bound to one game and
one capture target. Outlives individual matches.

Validity.description:
When a recommendation stops being true.

`invalidated_by` names change kinds; they are matched against the
`change_summary` of later observation envelopes. An empty
`invalidated_by` is a claim that nothing observable can falsify this
advice, which should be rare and deliberate.

expires_at.description:
Wall-clock expiry, when the advice is time-bounded rather than
state-bounded. `None` means it dies only on state change.

invalidated_by.description: Change kinds that kill this recommendation.
